title: QUIC Local Performance Lane Architecture
purpose: Define repo-local smoke and confidence performance lanes that combine BenchmarkDotNet developer feedback with ProtocolLab source-reference validation without changing benchmark semantics.
design_summary: The local performance lane wrapper owns profile selection, surface mapping, command provenance, and summary generation. BenchmarkDotNet remains the repo-local comparative feedback path, while ProtocolLab remains the end-to-end validation path through the existing source-reference helper. Smoke lanes use BDN Dry plus the smallest ProtocolLab source-reference run for mapped surfaces. Confidence lanes use BDN Short plus repeated ProtocolLab source-reference runs for mapped surfaces and stay report-only until stable thresholds exist. The wrapper never packs NuGet packages, publishes packages, uploads R2 bundles, or modifies ProtocolLab benchmark semantics.
edge_cases_and_constraints: Raw QUIC multiplex and duplex surfaces map to explicit ProtocolLab scenarios; raw send core is BDN-only unless the caller supplies a scenario.
Public API stream-transfer comparisons stay BDN-only by default because ProtocolLab raw QUIC and HTTP/3 scenarios are not one-to-one public facade workloads.
Confidence lane output is evidence only and must not fail on hard performance thresholds in this slice.
The local wrapper records commands and artifact paths so controlled-runner orchestration can reuse the same lane and surface vocabulary later.
risks: Developers can still overinterpret local confidence results as publishable benchmark claims, so the generated summary and docs must keep report-only wording visible.
Adding another local entry point can fragment workflow usage unless it delegates to the existing benchmark and ProtocolLab helpers instead of reimplementing them.
ProtocolLab source-reference runs remain subject to local machine noise; controlled compute nodes remain the future source for stronger evidence.

supplemental_sections.heading: Deterministic Scenario Driver Follow-Up
supplemental_sections.content: A later `QuicRuntimeScenarioDriver` test-harness slice should drive `QuicConnectionRuntime` with a test-controlled `FakeMonotonicClock`, explicit timer expirations, queued sends, ACK/loss events, and packet delivery without sockets. That future driver should prove exact scheduling and effect sequences before ProtocolLab validation, but it is intentionally out of scope for this performance-lane wrapper.
